call_structure: paired broadband tongue clicks, a few hundred microseconds long
notes: The one pteropodid genus known to echolocate. The clicks are made with the tongue, not the larynx, so this is an independent origin of echolocation rather than an inheritance from the other bats. Because the signal is a broadband click, a peak-frequency range describes it poorly and is not comparable with the peak frequency of a laryngeal call.
curation_note: Only R. aegyptiacus has been studied in detail (Holland et al. 2004); the other six species are assumed to click on genus-level grounds. Wing-generated clicks reported in a few other pteropodid genera (Boonman et al. 2014) are deliberately not asserted here.
